chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents in the year of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a year is too long. Whoever repents in the month of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a month is too long. Whoever repents on the day of his death, Allah forgives him.' Then he said, 'And indeed, a day is too long. Whoever repents when his soul has reached here' — and he pointed with his hand to his throat — 'Allah forgives him.'

key_terms.هَيْهَنَا: Here (indicating proximity, used for the throat)

ai.seo_question: How late can a person repent and still be forgiven by Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the expansive nature of divine mercy by progressively narrowing the window for repentance from a year to the final breath, culminating in the *mawt al-sirr* (death of the soul) at the throat. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hasarat* (regret) and the final opportunity for forgiveness even when the soul is ascending, reinforcing the concept that Allah's pardon is not strictly bound by early action but remains accessible until the very end of life.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 4.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Salamah Ṣāḥib al Sābirī,[1] from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Whoever repents in the year of his death, Allah forgives him.’ Then he said, ‘Verily a year is too long. Whoever repents in the month of his death, Allah forgives him.’ Then he said, ‘Verily a month is too long. Whoever repents on the day of his death, Allah forgives him.’ Then he said, ‘Verily a day is [still] long. Whoever repents an hour before his death, Allah forgives him.’ Then he said, ‘Verily [even] an hour is long. Whoever repents when his soul reaches here – and he pointed with his hand to his throat – Allah forgives him!’’[2]
